guarantees.claim: add_round_key_in is driven by state_q when add_rk_sel is ADD_RK_INIT or any unspecified value (default), by mix_columns_out when ADD_RK_ROUND, and by shift_rows_out when ADD_RK_FINAL.
guarantees.cond: always_comb triggered by any dependency change

formal.consequent: (add_rk_sel == ADD_RK_INIT) ? (add_round_key_in == state_q) : (add_rk_sel == ADD_RK_ROUND) ? (add_round_key_in == mix_columns_out) : (add_rk_sel == ADD_RK_FINAL) ? (add_round_key_in == shift_rows_out) : (add_round_key_in == state_q)

formal_sketch.antecedent: always_comb triggered by any dependency change
formal_sketch.consequent: (add_rk_sel == ADD_RK_INIT) ? (add_round_key_in == state_q) : (add_rk_sel == ADD_RK_ROUND) ? (add_round_key_in == mix_columns_out) : (add_rk_sel == ADD_RK_FINAL) ? (add_round_key_in == shift_rows_out) : (add_round_key_in == state_q)

uncertain_points.claim: If add_rk_sel takes an illegal value (not ADD_RK_INIT, ADD_RK_ROUND, or ADD_RK_FINAL), the default case assigns add_round_key_in = state_q, bypassing mix_columns_out or shift_rows_out transformations. The unique case warning does not halt the design; this path could be exploited by fault injection to weaken the cipher.
uncertain_points.cond: add_rk_sel receives an unexpected value due to a glitch or malicious attack
uncertain_points.risk: Untransformed state_q is fed directly into the round key addition, potentially enabling differential fault analysis or cryptanalytic attacks.

security_implications: The add_round_key_in mux default uses state_q for unspecified add_rk_sel. If an attacker can force add_rk_sel to an illegal value (e.g., via glitch), the round key addition receives the raw state_q instead of the shifted or mixed output, bypassing critical AES transformations. This could enable differential fault analysis or side-channel leakage of intermediate state. The unique case does not provide a hardware error response, creating a potential fault containment gap.
